unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft split the sentence so that 'The private secretary... and he saw his father' makes the son the grammatical subject. 'Then he said curtly' can therefore be read as the son speaking. The plan marks V6 as the Minister's speech.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The ambiguity exists in the source. 'Read it in silence' makes the father the natural speaker.

evidence.quote: he saw his father pick up a note from his desk and read it in silence. Then he said curtly
The private secretary had returned with the Minister from some social function, and he saw his father pick up a note from his desk
Then he said curtly: "Palmerston wants a quarrel!" Palmerston wanted a quarrel; he must not be gratified; he must be stopped.
